text:
Anna Park: FYI I'm seeing steady memory growth on long-context replay tests after the 3/11 runtime patch. Growth only shows up when using INT8 KV + longctx (>12k tokens).
Samir Patel: ugh, saw something similar in nightly e2e. Any repro steps yet? :eyes:
Anna Park: repro is a long chat workload (customer A), batching at 8, kernel selection falls back to the slower GEMM path for >2048 seq for that model. But the KV slab usage keeps climbing, not plateauing.
Jia Huang: can you dump the KV metrics when it happens? evicts, pages_in, pages_out, slot_alloc/forced_evictions, frag_pct?
Anna Park: pasted a short sample from local perf log:
```
kv_slots_total: 1048576
kv_slots_used: 812345
kv_evictions_forced: 480
kv_page_in_faults: 1240
kv_page_out_writes: 1198
kv_frag_percent: 28.7
int8_scale_drift_pct: 0.42
mem_rss_mb: 38720 -> 41260 over 30m
```
Samir Patel: frag pct ~29% is high, but not catastrophic. The odd bit is forced evictions low compared to page faults — suggests many cold slots are staying resident and causing page churn.
Jia Huang: hypothesis: the INT8 quantized layout reduces per-slot size enough that slab allocator switches bucket sizes and that triggers more cross-bucket fragmentation during longctx prepend/merge operations. Hot-cold migration might not be compacting buckets.
Anna Park: also noticed kernel fallback correlates: when kernel switches, latency spike + more KV allocs during warmup. Might be batching heuristic that increases prefix cache writes.
perf-bot: nightly/longctx/int8-replay failing rate increased by +3.2% since 1954540000 (runtime patch). Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/jobs/longctx-int8
Samir Patel: can we run a quick experiment: keep INT8 but force allocator to compact on threshold and disable hot-cold migration? I can instrument and run a 1h run.
Jia Huang: please capture per-slot age histogram and slot-temperature buckets. We should track"cold_to_hot" and "hot_to_cold" moves. Also record kernel selection trace (which kernel id used per step).
Anna Park: running now with compact_on_eviction=true, migration=false, batching.max_batch_size=6 (down from 8) to reduce prefix write amplification. Kickoff 1h at 1955555400.
Samir Patel: quick grep of the binary profiler showed this pattern: when fallback kernel is used, KV writes per-token go up ~1.9x. Possibly a different KV flush point in the runtime kernel handshake.
Jia Huang: interesting — that could explain extra writes leading to page-ins. If quant reduces slot width, allocator may place more slots per page but writes still target same hotspots. Increased per-token writes -> more page dirtiness -> more pageouts.
Anna Park: 30m into the run: mem_rss still rising but slope reduced. New sample:
```
kv_slots_used: 814100
kv_evictions_forced: 1120
kv_page_in_faults: 1340
kv_page_out_writes: 1325
kv_frag_percent: 30.1
mem_rss_mb: 40410 -> 40900 over 30m
int8_scale_drift_pct: 0.63
```
Samir Patel: eviction count increased (compact caused more churn) but mem slope reduced. So compact trades off CPU and write churn for memory stabilization.
Jia Huang: we need accuracy check too — I want to ensure compact/disable-migration doesn't change logits distribution for INT8. Can you run a small eval suite on the resulting model outputs (100 prompts) and track logit-MSE and top1/top5 deltas vs baseline FP16?
Anna Park: starting eval now, running 100 prompts across longctx patterns. Also capturing per-prompt latency p50/p95.
perf-bot: evict-compact-experiment started (run id: rc-195555-1).
Samir Patel: if compacting helps, might be worth adding an adaptive policy: compact at low CPU budgets, or when mem slope > x MB/min. But we should also look at improving kernel selection so it doesn't bounce. Maybe prefer the kernel that is KV-flush friendly when longctx workload detected.
Jia Huang: agree. Also check INT8 scale drift numbers — drift jumped in the initial runs. If compacting increases quantization noise (due to reordering?), could be a problem. We'll compare output accuracy.
Anna Park: eval finished: logit-MSE vs fp16 baseline: 0.0008 with compacting, 0.0006 on baseline run. Top1 accuracy delta: -0.3% for compacting, -0.2% without. p95 latency increased ~12ms.
Samir Patel: small accuracy hit and latency cost. Is that acceptable? For Dedicated customers maybe not. For lower tiers maybe we prefer stable mem.
Jia Huang: tradeoff judgement: compacting reduces long-term memory growth but adds CPU and slight quality regressions. Could be due to slot relocation changing quant scale contexts. Next step: try hybrid approach — compact only on high frag (>35%) and only for slots older than threshold. Also test an INT8 kernel variant that avoids prefix KV writes on fallback (kernel-level fix).
Anna Park: opened a short RFC and PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/3289 — contains flags: compact_on_high_frag, compact_age_threshold, kernel-pref-bias.
Samir Patel: suggested rollout plan: canary compact flags to 5% traffic for longctx models, gather mem slope and eval metrics for 24h. Also instrument kernel trace sampling for 1% of requests.
Jia Huang: I'll add the eval harness to the PR, and add a small test that asserts logit-MSE < 0.002 for compact path. Also add unit test for slot-temperature histogram after compaction.
Anna Park: thanks — I'll run the canary after PR merges. If we can also get a kernel patch to avoid write amplification that'd be ideal.
Samir Patel: noted — I'll spike on the kernel handshake tomorrow.
Anna Park: closing loop: main learnings -> compacting stabilizes memory but increases evictions and slightly affects accuracy; kernel fallback + batching heuristics amplify KV writes; adaptive compaction + kernel fix is next. :white_check_mark:
Jia Huang: +1. We'll track in the incident board if slope reappears.
perf-bot: rc-195555-1 completed: mem slope reduced by 42% during canary simulation. Metrics: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/rc-195555-1
Anna Park: filing follow-up ticket to test hybrid policy and kernel variant.
